items.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021
items.q: I worked a fair amount with Joe Wilder

ctx.x: Well I over the years have been lucky through this project I do to find myself briefly on a bandstand with people like Joe Wilder and of that generation. And I just remember almost like I need to pinch myself. Because here I am and there he is and I was hoping to do a good job but I think I just was filled with gratitude that that could happen, that this was happening.

Yeah. I mean look there’s — just listening – I worked a fair amount with Joe Wilder and just listening to him play is so wonderful, as is with so many of these musicians we’re talking about. There’s great joy and satisfaction of just being on the bandstand regardless of what you do, just listening to what comes out of their horn. And you’ve got a job to do and you do it as well as you can. And this experience of this collaborative art form © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

teaches you how to be in the moment and in the present. And to me the whole game that ties everything together is the cooperation or the successful cooperation of your conscious and subconscious. You know what I mean by that?
